comments:
Creating `/etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/50-dot.conf` with the following contents, and restarting resolved, works around the problem:

```
[Resolve]
DNSOverTLS=no
```

Hmm, the server you picked doesn't reply to our DNS-over-TLS requests at all, so things have to timeout. Not sure what we can do about this to speed this up. i mean falling back immediately or doing things in parallel in classic UDP mode defeats the point of DNS-over-TLS a bit, since we'd send requests in plaintext in that case..

> Hmm, the server you picked doesn't reply to our DNS-over-TLS requests at all, so things have to timeout. Not sure what we can do about this to speed this up. i mean falling back immediately or doing things in parallel in classic UDP mode defeats the point of DNS-over-TLS a bit, since we'd send requests in plaintext in that case..

Hm, but we're using `DNSOverTLS=opportunistic`, so why not just fall back immediately? This is best-effort protection against passive adversaries only, not protection against active attackers.

With `DNSOverTLS=yes` then it should obviously actually be secure and not fall back.

hmm, "immediately"? what does that even mean?

But yeah, I guess we could lower the timeout here in opportunistic mode to 3s. So the initial lookup will still be a bit slower, but not 30s.

Note that our [Fedora proposal to enable DNS over TLS](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/DNS_Over_TLS) was deferred to F36 over this issue, and is at risk of being dropped. If it's really just a matter of lowering a timeout somewhere, that would be a shame. ;)

review_comments: a comment explaining why those two settings are changed for UDP would be helpful
